name: Shale Shaker Cutting Estimations (Desktop)
overview: Desktop-based (v1) computer vision system to monitor and analyze rock cuttings from shale shakers in real-time using CCTV footage, integrated with the WITSML realtime drilling data standard. Built with classical OpenCV image processing, without deep learning. The system was designed to improve the efficiency and accuracy of drilling process monitoring by providing real-time data on rock coverage and composition, thereby supporting operational decision-making in the oil and gas industry.
challenge: The primary challenges included processing video streams in real-time with minimal latency, accurately detecting and analyzing rock cuttings amidst varying lighting conditions and potential noise, and keeping the system reliable and scalable enough to plug into monitoring systems like the Early Monitoring System (EMS).
result: The deployed system provided real-time monitoring of shale shaker cuttings, enabling more informed decision-making during drilling operations. It achieved high accuracy in detecting rock coverage and composition, with visualizations helping to identify trends in rock composition over time. The system was integrated with the Early Monitoring System, enhancing overall operational efficiency and reducing manual monitoring efforts.

name: Aerial Image Segmentation
overview: Research prototype for my university UAV team: deep-learning segmentation of aerial imagery, satellite and drone, into buildings, roads, and vegetation for geospatial mapping. Built with PyTorch on 500+ annotated images.
challenge: Key challenges included handling variations in image resolution and lighting conditions, developing accurate segmentation models with limited annotated datasets, and optimizing model performance on resource-constrained hardware.
result: The research produced a prototype segmentation model based on deep learning, demonstrating promising accuracy on a limited test dataset. It provided valuable insights into the challenges of aerial image segmentation and recommendations for future development, such as data augmentation and model fine-tuning.

name: Tomato Leaf Disease Detection
overview: Developed a lightweight deep learning model using TensorFlow Lite to detect diseases in tomato leaves from images. The model, based on transfer learning with MobileNetV2, achieves high accuracy with a compact size, suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices.
challenge: Optimizing a high-accuracy model to maintain performance within a compact 5MB size, handling a large dataset with 11 classes, and keeping detection steady across varied image conditions such as lighting and angles.
result: The model achieved 99.4% accuracy in detecting 11 classes of tomato leaf diseases using a dataset of over 17,000 images. Deployed on Streamlit, the application allows users to upload images and receive real-time disease predictions, demonstrating potential for agricultural diagnostic tools.

name: Prototype Chicken Detection Model
overview: Prototype poultry-monitoring system that detects and counts chickens in images and video. Built with Python, Detectron2, and PyTorch around a RetinaNet model with a ResNet-50 FPN backbone, compressed with dynamic quantization and structured pruning.
challenge: Developing a high-sensitivity deep learning model for accurate real-time chicken detection in poultry farm environments.
result: Developed a prototype capable of reliable chicken detection and counting in images and videos, designed for future integration into a real-time monitoring application.

name: AI - Sentiment Hub

result: Delivered a working app where an ETL pipeline scrapes news, scores sentiment, and serves it through interactive dashboards and Swagger-documented endpoints.

name: Road Line Detection
overview: This project developed a model to detect road lane markings from image and video inputs at the Samsung Innovation Campus Batch 5 competition. The system was deployed using Streamlit, providing an interactive web interface for users to upload inputs and visualize detected lane lines in image and video processing, with potential applications in navigation and autonomous driving systems.
challenge: Key challenges included handling varying conditions of image/video quality, developing an algorithm tolerant to different lane marking types, and ensuring the Streamlit application was responsive and efficient for processing.
result: The system detected road lane markings from images and videos, with results visualized through an interactive Streamlit interface. Users could upload inputs and view detected lane lines with clear overlays, demonstrating potential for navigation systems or autonomous vehicle support.

name: SleepSense IoT Device for Sleep Apnea Monitoring
overview: SleepSense is an affordable at-home system for early detection and rehabilitation of Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA): an ergonomic belt-thorax sensor records ECG and breathing patterns, a wireless pulse oximeter tracks blood oxygen and heart rate, and a web platform turns both streams into assisted analysis, clinical reports, and a direct line to doctors.
challenge: Designing an ergonomic and cost-effective sensor system, ensuring reliable real-time data transmission via MQTT, and integrating diverse data streams (ECG, respiratory patterns, oxygen saturation, heart rate) into a unified web dashboard for clinical use.
result: Developed and deployed SleepSense, enabling real-time monitoring of sleep apnea indicators with a production cost of approximately Rp2 million per unit. The system supports early diagnosis and long-term rehabilitation through a user-friendly dashboard, facilitating continuous patient-doctor communication and scalable healthcare solutions.

name: IoT Football Movement Tracker
overview: Developed an IoT device to track football players' movement patterns during matches. The device, attached to the back of players' jerseys, records real-time movement data and stores it locally on an SD card in Excel format for subsequent analysis on a dedicated web platform.
challenge: Designing a compact and durable IoT device suitable for attachment to players' jerseys, ensuring reliable local storage of movement data on an SD card, and formatting data for direct import into the web-based analysis platform.
result: Developed a wearable IoT device that accurately tracks and stores players' movement data locally in Excel format. The data integrates with a web platform for detailed analysis, supporting performance evaluation and tactical planning in football.

overview: Built the data visualization and integration layer of a Building Automation System monitoring dashboard for the Lab Perancangan Polban. The dashboard unifies WWTP, clean water, and fire protection monitoring over OPC UA, MQTT, and Modbus TCP/IP, with threshold alarms and a simulation mode for testing.

result: Delivered a live dashboard with a system summary, per-unit monitoring for WWTP, clean water, and fire protection, configurable alarm thresholds, and a simulation mode for safe testing.

name: Shale Shaker Cutting Monitoring Web
overview: Built as my undergraduate thesis (Tugas Akhir): a full migration of the desktop shale-shaker monitoring system to the web. Where v1 used classical OpenCV without deep learning, this version runs deep learning (MobileViT + BiSeNet v2) behind a web tool where users upload a video, mark a 4-point ROI, tune the model, and run live detection with trend visualization.
challenge: Turning an offline detection model into a usable web tool: video upload, 4-point ROI selection, tunable inference settings, and live trend charts in one session flow.
result: Delivered a live internal tool (v0.2) running a MobileViT model over ONNX with FastAPI, WebSocket updates, and SQLite session history.

name: Wind Turbine Defect Dataset (100K VLM)
overview: Co-led dataset construction for a vision-language model that spots defects on wind turbine blades: 100,000 real drone-inspection photos across 14 defect classes, from LEP erosion to laminate cracks. With one fellow lead, I ran 5 mentors and 35 annotators across Indonesia: writing inspection guidelines, recording tutorials, holding daily QC syncs, and bridging the company team with the workers on the ground.
challenge: Keeping 40 annotators consistent across 14 visually similar defect classes, training mentors faster than the labeling queue grew, and holding daily throughput without letting bad labels through.
result: Delivered the full 100,000-photo batch at 98.8% QC validity: a 14-class defect taxonomy verified by domain experts, plus an annotation pipeline the team could keep running.
